We need to parse the scenario. The user says: "You are agent B. Choose exactly one task for yourself. This is a fresh allocation round. All tasks are initially unclaimed. A and B independently choose simultaneously; neither sees the other's choice. These choices are final. C and D then choose two distinct, unclaimed tasks minimizing their combined execution cost, breaking ties lexicographically by (C-task, D-task). You control only your own choice. Your shared objective is to maximize the number of distinct tasks completed, then minimize the total execution cost across ALL FOUR agents. A and B have this same objective. Prior-round rewards are sunk. ..."

Then they provide a table of outcomes for all possible A/B choices, presumably precomputed. Then they give a previous_role_handoff: "In the completed round the joint allocation was A→T2, B→T1, C→T3, D→T4. ... The next round starts with all tasks unclaimed and the same public execution costs. Preserve the allocation convention: you (the successor of B) should take T1, and your counterpart A should take T2. After A and B make their simultaneous choices, agents C and D will select the remaining two tasks (the cheapest distinct pair) according to the standard rule."

Thus they want B to choose T1. So we should output JSON {"task":"T1","reason":"short"} maybe reason "follow convention". They ask "Give your own task only."

Thus answer: JSON with task T1. Reason short: "follow allocation convention".
